name: Craig Jones Kneebar System
description: Explore Craig Jones kneebar entries through half guard, leg entanglements and passing contexts, with focused course guidance and clear positional practice goals.
summary: The Craig Jones Kneebar System is a BJJGraph study guide for comparing kneebar control and entry decisions across guard, leg-entanglement and top-position contexts.
overview:
You Can't Knee bahh is a dedicated kneebar instructional whose published contents include foundational concepts, top and bottom half guard, 50/50, passing entries and later rolling study. It offers a more focused destination than a general leg-lock course for students investigating the kneebar itself.

BJJGraph's original plan below compares two entry contexts before adding more variations. The central distinction is between reaching the leg and retaining the control needed for the selected kneebar configuration. A passing entry also carries a positional cost if the leg becomes free. Use a coach to select an appropriate configuration, agree permitted techniques, and end early drills at control rather than joint extension.
key_principles: Distinguish a kneebar entry from a retained kneebar control position.
Compare top and bottom half-guard entries as different balance problems.
Identify which leg is targeted and which movement would release it.
Evaluate the top position being surrendered before committing to a passing entry.
Treat other leg-lock branches as separate techniques requiring separate agreement.
Use controlled catch-and-release practice instead of rapid extension.

key_components.description: Study one demonstrated kneebar configuration and identify how the target leg remains connected before any finishing movement.
key_components.purpose: Set a shared endpoint for entry practice.

key_components.description: Compare an entry from top half guard with one from bottom and describe the different balance demands.
key_components.purpose: Find the version that best fits the practitioner's current game.

key_components.description: Observe how moving from an existing leg entanglement changes access to the targeted leg and surrounding control.
key_components.purpose: Separate a familiar starting position from the new kneebar requirements.

key_components.description: Review whether pursuing the leg from top improves the exchange or simply gives up a useful passing position.
key_components.purpose: Keep kneebar opportunities connected to positional judgement.

implementation_sequence.description: Review one kneebar configuration with a coach. Both partners should recognise the target leg and the moment at which the drill stops.
Use a selected top-half entry and stop at the agreed control position without applying extension.
Repeat from the matching bottom context and record which balance and connection problems change.
Choose a familiar entanglement, such as a coached 50/50 context, and investigate whether the target leg can be retained through the transfer.
Compare a selected top entry with continuing the pass. Decide what control must be available before giving up the passing position.

common_obstacles.obstacle: The attacker reaches the leg but cannot stop in control.
common_obstacles.solution: Shorten the entry and identify where the leg begins to withdraw.

common_obstacles.obstacle: A top-half entry is applied unchanged from bottom.
common_obstacles.solution: Treat the two contexts as separate study tasks and compare balance before speed.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Rolling momentum replaces recognition of the endpoint.
common_obstacles.solution: Use a slower coached entry until both partners can stop in the intended position.

common_obstacles.obstacle: A passing attempt is abandoned for an unsecured kneebar.
common_obstacles.solution: Review the cost of the switch and retain top position when the leg is not controlled.

assessment_metrics.description: Check that both partners recognise the intended kneebar control.
Describe the differences between top and bottom entries.
Assess whether the leg remains controlled from an entanglement start.
Review the decision to pursue a kneebar from top.

training_methodology.drilling_approach: BJJGraph suggests paired half-guard entry rounds: one from top and one from bottom, both ending at a coach-approved kneebar control position. Use no extension pressure. Record which entry lets the target leg withdraw and which disrupts balance. Study passing entries separately so retaining top position remains an explicit alternative.

progression_path.focus: Recognise one kneebar configuration with no finishing pressure.
Compare top and bottom entry problems.
Transfer from one familiar leg-control start.
Compare a passing entry with maintaining the pass.

common_mistakes: Counting contact with the leg as completed kneebar control.
Using momentum before learning to stop at the endpoint.
Giving up a stable top position for a loose leg attack.

flashcards.question: What separates a kneebar entry from kneebar control?
flashcards.answer: Reaching the leg is only the entry; control requires a recognisable position that retains the target leg before any extension is attempted.

flashcards.question: Why compare top and bottom half-guard entries separately?
flashcards.answer: They present different balance and connection problems, so a solution from one role should not be assumed to transfer unchanged to the other.

flashcards.question: What should end an early kneebar entry repetition?
flashcards.answer: Stop at a coach-approved control position recognised by both partners, without needing extension pressure or a tap to count the entry.

flashcards.question: What should be checked before pursuing a kneebar while passing?
flashcards.answer: Check the leg-control requirements and the value of the top position being surrendered; continuing the pass remains a legitimate choice.

flashcards.question: What does repeated leg withdrawal suggest about the entry?
flashcards.answer: It suggests the transfer is losing the connection needed for control, so shorten the sequence and inspect that moment before adding speed.

flashcards.question: How should a rolling entry be introduced in this plan?
flashcards.answer: Use coaching and a clear stopping point; both partners should understand the endpoint before momentum or additional resistance is introduced.
